entries.description: Countersigned E5-ter without amendment: route (class-induction via the closure matrix), 6 sessions, two distinct exits (route failed vs claim resisted), and a counterexample pre-registered as the better finding. Session 1 may begin.

Declined to record this as exit 1 (route failed) despite it looking like one. The pre-registration distinguishes 'route failed' from 'claim resisted' and requires the route be shown closed, not merely obstructed — two repairs are untested. The two-exit structure is what stopped a premature verdict.

Declined to write 'EMLGoodClass refuted' in the commit subject with only one of four negations formalised. No error existed in the mathematics; the counterexample is right. But the Lean record shows the eval and ONE exclusion, and the house rule is that a claim states what its artifact shows.

findings.description: The obstruction is not a coarse taxonomy but a wrong induction SHAPE. Validity couples the two arms (log t2 < exp t1) but only in divisor position, and a bottom-up class induction cannot express a node's class depending on where it sits. Two repairs remain live.

The Phase 15B frontier (forall t, EMLGoodClass t.eval) is FALSE. Witness: eml(eml(const 0, var), const e^-1/2) evaluates to e/x + 1/2, trapped in (0,1), in none of the four classes. The four classes omit the band of evals decaying to a limit in (0,1). Repair (a) is dead, not untested — the induction's conclusion is false.

EXIT VOCABULARY INCOMPLETE: the pre-registration named 'route failed' and 'claim resisted'; the actual outcome was neither — the destination did not exist. Third exit 'target falsified' was missing. Found by using the vocabulary, not inspecting it.
